title: Contineum, J&J's depression drug fails to meet mid-stage trial goal
summary: Contineum Therapeutics said on Monday an experimental depression drug it developed with Johnson & ​Johnson failed to meet the main goal ‌of a mid-stage study.

contentHtml:
Sept 15 (Reuters) - Contineum Therapeutics

(CTNM.O), opens new tab

said on Monday an experimental depression drug it developed with Johnson & ​Johnson

(JNJ.N), opens new tab

failed to meet the main goal ‌of a mid-stage study.

Here are the details:

Sign up here.

  • The trial was testing the drug, JNJ-5120 or PIPE-307, in patients with ​major depressive disorder, or MDD.

  • The trial measured improvements ​on a standard depression rating scale at ⁠day five compared with a placebo, but the ​drug did not achieve the required efficacy endpoint.

  • Shares ​of Contineum fell nearly 8% in after-hours trading.

  • The treatment is being developed by healthcare giant Johnson & Johnson under a global ​licensing agreement. J&J is continuing to review ​the broader data from the study to decide the next ‌steps ⁠for the medicine.

  • The company said the treatment was well-tolerated and showed no new safety signals.

  • The drug targets a brain receptor called M1 and was designed ​to work ​quickly, within ⁠days, unlike many antidepressants that can take weeks to show an effect.

  • In 2025, ​a study testing the same compound, ​PIPE-307, in ⁠multiple sclerosis patients also failed to show a benefit.

  • MDD affects more than 21 million adults in ⁠the ​U.S. each year, making it one ​of the most common mental health conditions in the country.

Reporting ​by Kamal Choudhury in Bengaluru; Editing by Arun Koyyur
